title: Submergence of Sundaland
summary: Following the Last Glacial Maximum, rapid post-glacial sea-level rise and meltwater pulses submerged the vast Sunda Shelf, which had connected mainland Southeast Asia with Sumatra, Java, and Borneo. Flooding over half of Sundaland by approximately 9,500 years ago, this marine transgression created the contemporary Indonesian archipelago, severed terrestrial migration corridors, drove human and faunal relocations, and abruptly intensified regional monsoon rainfall.

uncertainty.note: Marine transgression accelerated during Meltwater Pulse 1A (~14.5–14.0 ka) and 1B (~11.5–11.0 ka), with extensive shelf flooding and Java Sea opening dated to approximately 9.5 ka (Griffiths et al. 2010; Peng et al. 2023).

as_recorded.value: flooding of the Sunda Shelf ~9500years ago

where.historical_name: Sundaland continental shelf, late Pleistocene to early Holocene; no polities existed

importance.justification: Drowned a subcontinent-sized landmass, created the modern maritime Southeast Asian archipelago, and reshaped human and ecological dispersal routes.
